## Govern

**2026-11-06, E9.1, change.** Card E9.1 added Govern's knowledge profile: org takes only user and document sources at a 0.8 floor, team and org require review, shared scopes hold no episodic records, and the conflict and validity lints are listed. Roadmap epic E9: Govern needs a policy for trusted organisational memory before its screens (E9.3) and dogfood (E9.5). The profile loads; 13 fixture writes get the decision, status and rule the fixture names; an org candidate is read only after a reviewer promotes it; a model-written note cannot be promoted into org; an item past its window is excluded. 18 tests pass. `engram --policy packages/pi-package/profiles/knowledge.yaml` governs with it; card PX3 ships the folder in the pi package.[^1][^2][^3][^4]

**2026-11-13, E9.1, finding.** Review of PR #30 found three gaps: the fixture checked no deny reason; the model-note promotion test accepted an ask and named a reviewer it never used; nothing tested that tool content admitted to team cannot be promoted into org. A denial for the wrong clause passed, and org's first-hand rule was proven only for direct writes, not promotion (ADR 0026). Every fixture case now names its reason; the model-note test requires deny under `profile.knowledge/write/org`; a new test reviews a tool item into team, then has a reviewer promote it to org: denied. 19 tests pass; allowing `tool` in org fails 3. The profile comment now says contradiction is listed as in strict only, and that no conflict lint runs until L1 (duplicate) and L3 (contradiction) land.[^5][^6][^7][^8]

**2026-11-21, E2.9, failure.** ADR 0039 put a fingerprint of the first and last four characters of a matched secret into the event's reason, which would write a short secret into the log in full (review finding AP-2). The design was taken from the absorbed guards without asking what it means for a permanent, append-only log. A secret of eight characters or fewer would be logged whole and a card number would lose only eight digits, against the ADR's own sentence that the log must not hold the secret. The reason now names the rule's kind and the match's length, and no character of the value. A keyed hash for correlating repeats is left as a later decision. Card E2.9's tests assert that no reason contains any substring of a planted secret.[^9][^10]

**2026-11-21, E2.11, failure.** ADR 0040 and card E2.11 said every surface in the repository declares its source; the HTTP API does not (review finding AP-1). The sentence was written from the comment on `withPlaneProvenance`, which names the pi extension, the CLI and adoption, without opening the server's routes. The ADR and the card now name which surfaces set a source, state that HTTP callers choose their own, and say that the floor reaches only callers that send none. Card E2.7 lists each surface with file and line instead of assuming the list. A claim about every surface is checked surface by surface before it is written. See the finding entry on the HTTP source.[^11][^12][^13]

**2026-11-28, RD1, failure.** The item-page e2e "shows sam, who cannot read the note, no node, edge or count that reveals it" failed in the orchestrator's run: on the team item's page it found no `lineage:TEAM>CHECKLIST` edge. It was not RD1 over-hiding. In process, sam's read, by-id read and events all give the checklist the lineage `[TEAM]`, with only the note dropped, which ADR 0047's rule and ADR 0034 decision 9 require. The graph's edges depend only on that lineage. The test read the edges once, right after the node count settled, and React Flow draws edges after it measures the nodes. Before: 2 of 11 full-file runs failed at line 365, and 5 runs of that test alone passed. The test now polls for the lineage edge, with the same expectation. After: 8 of 8 full-file runs passed (13 tests each). No code changed. Nothing further.[^14][^15][^16]

## Twin

**2026-11-06, E9.2, change.** Card E9.2 added Twin's profile (ADR 0021): a person scope that takes everything the person and their agent remember, a role scope that takes only work knowledge and procedures from first-hand and tool sources, a role context that reads no person scope, and no default grants. Roadmap epic E9: Twin needs its scope split as a policy before its screens (E9.4), dogfood (E9.5) and offboarding (E9.7). The profile loads; in the fixture a teammate reads only the item a live, class-scoped grant gives them, nothing after it expires; a role context reads the role and not its holder's person scope; a grant without class or expiry, a model write to a role and an episodic role record are denied; an agent cannot widen person memory into a role. 8 tests pass. E9.7 hands role scopes over and erases person scopes under this profile.[^17][^18][^19][^20]

**2026-11-06, E9.7, change.** Card E9.7 added `offboard`: the leaver's items in each handed-over role scope become the successor's, the person scope is erased from the store, the projection and the log's copies, and a deletion report names what was done and what it cannot reach. ADR 0021 and ADR 0010: a role passes to a successor, and person-scope erasure is the one hard deletion, with a report. Under the twin profile, Sam reads both role items after Dana leaves and may rewrite them; none of Dana's five person items is in the store, the projection, a rebuilt projection or any event's text; an agent, or a colleague outside the person scope, is refused with one deny event. 6 acceptance and 4 replay tests pass. No surface calls it yet; a CLI command and the Twin screens (E9.4) are follow-ups.[^21][^22][^23][^24][^25]

**2026-11-13, E9.2, finding.** The review pass over PR #31 (the twin profile) found no defect to fix. Every open PR is reviewed before merge: the profile against ADR 0021 and decision D4, the fixture against the read filter in packages/core/src/policy/evaluate.ts, and the tests against docs/conventions/testing.md. The profile parses; the role row never reads a person scope; grants admit only while live and of the item's class; the fixture runs through the real Plane over the fake store. The acceptance command passes, 8 of 8, and `make lint-docs` and biome on the touched files pass. The profile's `schema_version: 0` matches main. Nothing changes in the profile. Whichever of this PR and the schema PR merges second still bumps the profile's schema version.[^26][^27][^28]

**2026-11-13, E9.7, finding.** The review of PR #33 confirmed two defects in `offboard` and one gap in its tests, and fixed them test first. A handover store failure threw without an event (AGENTS.md rule 3). Erasure deleted every ref an erased item held, even one an item outside the person scope also holds, deleting that item's bytes. The redaction and the explanation-row removal ran only on SQLite, and no test read before offboarding, so the row removal was never exercised. A failed handover now appends one deny event (`engram/write/store-failure`) and throws before erasing; a shared ref is kept and reported. offboard-edges.test.ts, 5 tests, runs the erasure on SQLite and embedded Postgres and finds the same log; each fix, broken on purpose, fails its test. ADRs 0010 and 0021 amended (the decision entry of the same day).[^29][^30][^31]

**2026-11-13, failure.** When the store failed to delete an item during offboarding (card E9.7), the plane still erased it from the projection and the log under a reason saying "deleted from the store", and adoption (`adoptStoreItems`, card E8.2) then re-imported its plaintext. The erasure only collected delete failures for the report and erased regardless. Adoption treats a store record the projection lacks as new. Fixed in the spirit of the handover failure path: such an item is not erased this run, gets one deny event under `engram/write/store-failure` naming the error, and is listed with its ref under `store_failures`; a rerun after the store recovers erases it. Each erase event now says whether its item was deleted, kept because an item outside the person scope shares its ref, or had no store record. A deletion report with `store_failures` means offboarding is not finished.[^32][^33]

**2026-11-13, failure.** Offboarding's erasure (card E9.7) left an erased item's content hash and provenance hash in the reasons of lint events (card L1). E9.7's redaction rewrote only events that carry an item; L1's lint events carry an item id and put their evidence (a duplicate's strict content hash, a source-changed finding's recorded and current hashes) in `reason`. The deletion report's `not_reached` text and ADR 0010 both promised those hashes were gone. Reproduced under the twin profile: two equal person notes, a lint, an offboarding, and the log still held the hash. Fixed: every lint event about an erased item, or naming one or a hash of one of its versions, keeps its lint id, severity and rule and reads `<lint_id> (<severity>): [erased]`. Replay and rebuild still equal the incremental projection on SQLite and embedded Postgres. New evidence in a reason must join the redaction.[^34][^35]

**2026-11-13, failure.** An adversarial recheck of PR #41 found its adoption skip and its read re-check wrong. Adoption skipped any erased id, but the files adapter derives an imported id from the file name, so a successor's adoption and other people's same-named folders were hidden forever, rewrites were never governed, no event was written, and an adoption queued behind the offboarding wrote the erased bytes back. The read dropped erased items after scoring and the limit, leaving short reads and deflated relevance, and bound one parameter per item. Adoption now refuses, in the write queue with a deny event, only a record holding content erased and left in the store. The read re-checks the projection under its lock with a parameter-free query before filtering, scoring and the limit. Both were broken on purpose to show their tests fail. Letta's permanent errors and a surface for `left_in_store` are backlogged.[^36][^37]

**2026-11-13, failure.** The adversarially verified review of PR #41 found three defects in its own fixes. The keep-back path for failed deletes treated the files adapter's ReadOnlyItemError, thrown for every adopted Claude Code memory file, as transient, so offboarding never erased adopted files. Lint redaction matched any erased item's hash, so it erased duplicate and source-changed findings about surviving items sharing that text or source. The read's re-check ran before its transaction took the log's lock, so an erasure by another process could still land between them. Adapter contract gains `NotDeletableError`; a permanent refusal erases and reports `left_in_store`. A hash counts only when no survivor holds it. The re-check moved inside the transaction. The adoption and read parts were redone after a recheck (`docs/log/2026-11-13-post-merge-failure-pr41-recheck.md`). Each fix was broken on purpose to show its test fails. Tests of erasure now run over the real files adapter too.[^38][^39]

**2026-11-21, D1, decision.** The fifty sessions go in a subfolder, `fixtures/sessions/d1/`, with an `index.json`. They do not sit at the top level of `fixtures/sessions/` beside a `.expected.json` each. Card PX2's replay test reads every top-level `fixtures/sessions/*.jsonl` and expects its `engram.policy` and `engram.call` entries. A recorder fixture has neither, so fifty top-level files would break that test. PX2's two fixtures are unchanged, and `git status` shows nothing else in `fixtures/` changed. `make fixtures` empties and rewrites only `fixtures/sessions/d1`. A later card that globs `fixtures/sessions/` recursively must skip `d1/`, or read its index.[^281][^282]

## Plane

**2026-10-17, milestone.** The body of knowledge for the repository was written before any code: operating manual, ADR 0001 (pi as base), documentation and testing conventions, proposed ADRs 0002 to 0023, the step-0 task list, the readings list and the glossary. So the first card is worked under the conventions rather than before them, and so the thesis can be assembled from the log instead of from memory. Files listed under evidence. No measurements yet. Step 0 starts at S0.1. ADRs 0002 to 0023 are decided in S0.13.[^375][^376][^377][^378]

**2026-10-17, decision.** The lead removed the PR size limit: AGENTS.md rule 10 no longer caps a PR at 400 changed lines or asks for a card to be split first, and the card prompt pattern no longer says "Keep the diff under 400 lines". The limit was forcing cards such as S0.3 (518 changed lines, mostly tests) to be split into halves that are not useful on their own. Rule 10 now reads "One task card per PR. Title is the card id and its goal." The same sentence is gone from `docs/tasks/step-0.md` and `.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md`. One card per PR still holds; reviewers judge size case by case.[^379][^380][^381]

**2026-10-17, S0.1, failure.** Running `biome migrate --write` on Biome 2.5.15 to replace the deprecated `rules.recommended: true` produced `rules.preset: "none"`, which turns every lint rule off. The deprecation notice asked for the migration; the result was only caught because the config was read back after migrating. With `preset: "none"`, `make lint` passed while enforcing nothing. After setting `preset: "recommended"`, a probe file with `any`, `==`, an inner `var` and an unused variable produced four diagnostics (`noExplicitAny`, `noDoubleEquals`, `noInnerDeclarations`, `noUnusedVariables`). Any future Biome migration is followed by reading `biome.json` back and running a probe before merging.[^382][^383]

**2026-10-17, S0.1, change.** Step-0 task S0.1 bootstrapped the monorepo: pnpm workspace with nine package stubs (core, adapters, pi-extension, runner, bench, mcp, cli, server, ui), a uv workspace with `research` as its member, Biome, TypeScript, Vitest, fast-check, ruff, mypy, pytest, Hypothesis, a Makefile and a GitHub Actions workflow running `make lint` and `make test`. Every later card runs its acceptance command through the Makefile, so the commands must exist before the first real card. Before: `make test` failed with `Command "vitest" not found`. After: `make test` passes on an empty suite (Vitest with `passWithNoTests`, pytest exit code 5 accepted) and `make lint` passes. TypeScript is 7.0.2, not the 5.x in ADR 0019, on the lead's instruction; ADR 0019 is amended. Unimplemented targets exit 2 naming their card. Windows members need GNU make (`winget install ezwinports.make`).[^384][^385][^386][^387]

**2026-10-17, S0.1, failure.** The first CI run of S0.1 failed before any step ran because `astral-sh/setup-uv@v10` does not resolve. The workflow used floating major tags for every action. `actions/checkout`, `actions/setup-node` and `pnpm/action-setup` publish them; `astral-sh/setup-uv` stopped at `v7`, and its current release is only tagged `v10.3.0`. Run 39048041089 failed in "Set up job" with "unable to find version `v10`". The workflow now pins `astral-sh/setup-uv@v10.3.0`. Before adding an action, check that the tag exists (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/matching-refs/tags/v`).[^388][^389]

**2026-10-17, S0.2, milestone.** Step-0 task S0.2 completed the body of knowledge and the harness setup: `make lint-docs` (em dashes in prose, CLAUDE.md equals AGENTS.md, log entry field set), a log template at `docs/log/_template.md`, the card prompt pattern and session rules in `.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md`, and `.claude/` settings and commands mirroring the three pi prompts. CLAUDE.md was described as a symlink, which is unreliable on Windows, so it is now a copy that CI compares byte for byte. pi 1.3.0 in RPC mode (`get_commands`, run with `-a`) lists `adr`, `card` and `log-entry` as project prompts; its resource loader finds one context file, AGENTS.md, so the copy is not loaded twice. `make lint-docs` passes, and fails on a seeded em dash, a drifted CLAUDE.md and an entry missing fields. S0.3 hardens the log validator and adds the PR checks.[^390][^391][^392][^393][^394]

**2026-10-17, S0.3, change.** Step-0 task S0.3 added the convention gates: `check-pr.ts` (the PR body has an `Acceptance:` line with a real command, and the diff adds a valid docs/log entry), a full log validator (field set, enums, real dates, H1 to H5, evidence paths exist, supersedes points at an entry, body sections in order, at most 150 words), fixture PRs under `fixtures/ci/`, and `conventions.yml` running the gate on every pull request. AGENTS.md rule 14 and the documentation convention say CI rejects a PR without a log entry or an acceptance command. `make lint-docs PR=fixtures/ci/pr-no-log` fails with "PR diff must add or change an entry under docs/log/"; `PR=fixtures/ci/pr-valid` passes; both are asserted in `scripts/test/fixtures-ci.test.ts`. All seven existing entries pass. Edits to existing entries are not yet detected; immutability is enforced in review only.[^395][^396][^397][^398][^399][^400]

**2026-10-17, S0.3, failure.** On Windows, the check scripts crashed with a libuv assertion (`!(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING)`, `src\win\async.c`) when they called `process.exit(1)` straight after writing problems to stderr. `process.exit` tears the process down while the stderr pipe write is still pending; the scripts ran under make, whose stderr is a pipe. The gate still failed, but with exit code 127 and a crash message instead of exit code 1. Setting `process.exitCode` and returning lets the write finish; the same run now exits 1 with only the problem line. Scripts in this repository set `process.exitCode` and never call `process.exit` after writing output.[^401][^402]

**2026-10-17, S0.5, failure.** The S0.5 session fixture recorded on Windows failed on Linux CI. Three values were not stable: the faux provider's default API id embeds a timestamp and a random suffix; the system prompt carries the temporary working directory with forward slashes; and the faux provider estimates token usage from prompt length, which depends on that path. The first two were caught locally across repeated runs; usage was caught by CI, where input token counts differed by seven per call. The scripted model now takes a fixed API id, and the normalizer replaces both path spellings and the usage object. Session fixtures are accepted only after a green run on both Windows and Linux.[^403][^404]

**2026-10-17, S0.5, finding.** Step-0 task S0.5 pinned pi 1.3.0 and proved the interception points in a pi SDK session with a scripted model: tool_call blocks an org-scoped memory_write, context tags memory, every decision is an `engram.event` custom entry, and store commands are blocked in user_bash and in the model's bash tool. ADR 0001 rests on these events behaving as documented. tool_call, context and appendEntry behaved as documented; 15 tests pass. Three differences: `createAgentSession` has no `extensionFactories` option (it moved to `DefaultResourceLoader`); `session.executeBash` never emits user_bash, only the interactive and RPC hosts do; user_bash has no block result, so blocking returns a replacement result. The runner must emit user_bash itself. The context tag is request-local; the session keeps untagged results.[^405][^406][^407][^408]

**2026-10-22, change.** A file-backed event log now runs in WAL mode with a five-second busy timeout, and the outermost transaction begins IMMEDIATE. The final step-0 review found that two processes appending to one log would get "database is locked" at once, because the sequence read ran inside a deferred savepoint with no timeout. Tests show the pragmas are set on a file database, and that two connections appending in turn to one file keep a dense sequence 0 to 3. The 500-sequence replay property still passes. Several runner processes can share one log file; nested transactions remain savepoints.[^409][^410]

**2026-10-22, change, H4.** The Adapter contract now says `history` returns every distinct version under a ref, and the conformance suite checks that rewriting identical content adds no version. The final step-0 review found the fake skipped identical rewrites while the contract said every version written. A store that treats an identical rewrite as a no-op, as Mem0 does with NOOP, could not meet the stricter wording. The fake passes; a fake that records every write fails the new case. Real adapters are held to distinct versions only.[^411][^412]

**2026-10-22, S0.10, failure.** The test proving the pi-import lint rule timed out in the full suite although it passed alone. It spawned Biome three times per package; under a parallel `make test` each spawn took about two seconds, past Vitest's 5-second default. Two earlier designs also failed: Biome 2.5 in stdin mode exits 1 for a clean file without `--write` and prints no diagnostics with it, and probe files under `.gitignore` are skipped unless `--vcs-use-ignore-file=false` is passed. One Biome run per package over three probe files, counting three diagnostics, with a 30-second timeout; two full runs passed 114 of 114. Tests that spawn tools set an explicit timeout.[^413][^414]

**2026-10-22, S0.10, change.** Step-0 task S0.10 added the model call layer: `ModelCall` and `requestHash` in core; a scripted `ModelCall` keyed on the request hash that fails loudly on a miss; `cached()` with the ADR 0017 key, usage capture and an `ENGRAM_OFFLINE=1` refusal; a pi-ai backed `ModelCall` in the runner; and a Biome rule rejecting pi imports in core and adapters. AGENTS.md rules 4, 6 and 7: the plane never calls a model, and every call is seeded and cached. 13 runner tests: a second identical call makes zero underlying calls, offline mode throws on a miss and answers a hit, usage is recorded for hits and misses, and file cassettes survive a new process. Three tests show the import rule fires in core and adapters, not in the runner. `ModelCall` is a type in core, so lints and the distiller receive it without importing the runner.[^415][^416][^417][^418][^419]

**2026-10-22, S0.11, change, H4.** Step-0 task S0.11 added the `Adapter` contract (read, write, delete, list, optional search and history, capability flags), a complete in-memory fake, and the conformance suite as an exported `conformance(name, factory)` that adapters A1 to A3 call from their own tests. ADR 0013 and H4: every store is held to one contract, first on a fake, then in CI service containers. 32 cases pass on the fake with and without its optional methods: round trip, idempotent write, store_ref opacity (serialisable, foreign refs refused), delete visibility, scope-exact list, search never crossing the scope filter, recall on a five-item corpus, and history in order. Mutations that ignore the scope filter or skip deletion fail it. Refs are keyed by item id in the fake; real adapters may key differently because the plane never builds a ref.[^420][^421][^422][^423]

**2026-10-22, S0.11, failure.** The S0.11 commit was made and pushed while `make lint` failed on a TypeScript error in the conformance suite. The command chain ran lint, tests and the commit in sequence without stopping on the lint exit code; the tests passed, so the commit went through. The base fixture was typed as the whole MemoryItem union, so spreading it with new string content did not type-check. Commit 7515b0d typed it as a knowledge item; `make lint` passed afterwards. Commits are chained on `make lint && make test`, so a failing gate stops the commit; CI would also have caught it.[^424][^425]

**2026-10-22, S0.7, change.** Step-0 task S0.7 added schema v0 in Zod 4 for MemoryItem, MemoryEvent, Policy, Grant, Explanation and LintFinding, following `docs/architecture.md`; `make api` exports JSON Schema to `sdk/schema/` and generates Python TypedDicts in `research/engram_types/`, and `make api-check` fails on a dirty tree. ADR 0003: the event log is the source of truth and store state is a projection that must be rebuildable. 9 unit tests and a fast-check property over 500 random event sequences (seeded from the test name): the rebuilt projection equals the incremental one. Replaying events in reverse breaks it after 6 runs with a shrunk two-write counterexample and the seed printed, so the test can fail. **2026-10-22, change.** Schema v0 changed in three ways from the final step-0 review: structured content must be JSON (a shared `JsonValue` definition exported beside the contracts), `Provenance` gains the optional `model` that ADR 0004 lists, and every exported schema carries a title so the generated Python types are named after their contracts. A Date or NaN in content changed on storage; ADR 0004's accepted option named a field the schema lacked; two generated types were called `Model`. New tests failed first and pass: content values JSON cannot carry are rejected, a model-written fixture validates in Zod and JSON Schema, and each Python module defines its contract's name. `schema_version` stays 0: v0 was never released or persisted, so no migration exists to write. **2026-10-22, change.** Fixes for the eight important findings of the final step-0 review: allowed changing events must carry their item under the same id; `Db.transaction` refuses an async body; the Adapter contract moved to core and the Plane is asynchronous; the conformance suite tests an empty scope filter, skips missing optional methods visibly and moves full recall to an opt-in lexical suite; the cassette cache treats only a missing file as a miss, writes atomically and deduplicates calls in flight; pi subpath imports are rejected; ADRs 0002 to 0023 are marked pending the lead's review. Each would have cascaded into the E2 and A cards or misattributed decisions in the thesis. Every fix has a test that failed first; `make test` passes. Seventeen minor findings are deferred and listed in the step-0 report.[^441][^442][^443][^444][^445][^446]

**2026-10-25, A1, failure.** After `pnpm add mem0ai@3.3.1`, Mem0's local vector store could not open: pnpm 10 ignored the install script of `better-sqlite3`, so its native binding was never built. `mem0ai/oss` imports `better-sqlite3` for its default in-memory vector store, and pnpm 10 runs no dependency build script unless the workspace allows it. pnpm printed "Ignored build scripts: better-sqlite3@12.11.1". Allowing the build (`allowBuilds: better-sqlite3: true` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) fetched a prebuilt binary for Node 24 on Windows x64 and the store opened. `better-sqlite3` is now a direct dependency of `packages/adapters` at an exact version. A machine with no prebuilt binary for its platform needs a C++ toolchain for node-gyp.[^447][^448]

**2026-10-25, A1, change, H4.** Card A1 added the Mem0 adapter on open-source Mem0 (`mem0ai` 3.3.1, `mem0ai/oss`) with Mem0's own SQLite vector store, in memory or in a file. ADR 0013 holds every store to one contract; Mem0 is the first real store. Each MemoryItem is one Mem0 memory added with `infer: false`, so Mem0 stores the content verbatim and no model is called. The item rides in Mem0 metadata with `engram_id` and `engram_scope`, which `list` and `search` filter on. The embedder is injected; tests use a deterministic hashing embedder, and Mem0's model slot refuses every call. Telemetry is forced off and Mem0 writes nothing to its home directory. The Mem0 entry passes all 15 applicable conformance cases offline; the two history cases skip because the adapter offers no history. Search quality depends on the injected embedder, so Mem0 is not opted into lexical full recall.[^449][^450][^451][^452]

The first mem0 case paid the `mem0ai/oss` load inside its beforeEach factory, the same cost that timed out mem0.test.ts. **2026-10-25, A1, change.** The beforeAll hook of mem0.test.ts now builds one throwaway Mem0 instance, under the fetch stub and the temporary MEM0_DIR, with a 60 s hook timeout. **2026-10-28, E2.3, failure.** The first version of the test that a failed store write does not stall the write queue (finding N2) was wrong. Behind the queue, the store is called later, after the fault is cleared, so the "failing" write succeeded. The fault now fails by item id, not by when it is set. The test fails against a queue that does not swallow rejections, and passes against the real one. In a test of queued work, set faults by what they apply to, not by when they are set.[^619][^620]

**2026-10-29, A2, failure.** The race test written for review finding R2-1 accepted any number of items deleted by user commits as git's stale-index race. It recorded every deleted item as "reverted" without checking that the deleting commit raced the Engram commit that added it, so a defect that un-stages each item after its commit passed it 3 of 3 runs (the verifier's mutation, N2). At most one reverted item per run is allowed, and the deleting user commit's parent must be the `engram: write <id>` commit of that item; the mutation now fails the test every run. A tolerance in a test is bounded by the evidence for it.[^643]

**2026-10-29, A2, failure.** The first runs of the new race test failed twice for reasons other than R2-1: once an intent-to-add entry stayed in the index after a refused write, and once the user's commit deleted an item Engram had just committed. The first: the restore's reset met the user's `index.lock` and failed (now reported, R2-3). The second is git's own race (see the finding on it). Git calls refused for `index.lock` are now retried for about two seconds before they count as failures; the test tolerates exactly the second case, naming it, and asserted ten passes in ten runs afterwards; the R2-1 mutation still fails it. **2026-10-29, A2, failure.** The first conformance run of the Letta adapter failed all 42 of its cases with `TypeError: realpath.native is not a function`. **2026-10-29, A2, failure.** The Letta adapter reported writes as stored that were never committed by Engram (review finding R2-1, critical). A write staged its files with `git add`, so a user's `git commit` running at that moment committed them; Engram's commit then found nothing to commit, and the adapter counted that as success. Reproduced by the reviewer with two writer processes and a user commit loop (16 writes, 12 Engram commits, four user commits holding engram files). Fixed: new files are staged intent-to-add, which another client's commit never takes, the commit is `--only` on the two paths, and any commit failure is a failure. `race.test.ts` fails when the old staging and success rule are restored. Engram never stages an item's content where another client can commit it.[^655]

**2026-10-29, E1.1, failure.** The first Postgres backend let a transaction half-commit after its connection dropped, and let a timed-out writer keep the log's advisory lock. postgres.js reconnects transparently: after `pg_terminate_backend`, the next statements ran in a new session with no BEGIN, no lock and no search path, and the final COMMIT was only a warning. Separately, terminating the worker on a client timeout does not stop a busy backend, so its transaction and lock outlived the Db. Found by the independent review; the first suite never dropped a connection or timed out in a transaction. Both are now tests: the terminate probe expects the transaction to throw and no rows in either schema, and a second writer must get the lock within 3 s of the first one's timeout. A backend test suite needs fault cases (dropped connection, failed begin, timeout in a transaction), not only the happy contract.[^694][^695]

**2026-11-20, RV5, change.** Core judges a read's access (status, ttl, grants), and stamps its ts, never earlier than the log's last event (`accessTime`); an earlier named time becomes the read's history `valid_at`, recorded apart from ts. The timeline route uses the same time (finding RV-CORE-3, at the coordinator's request). The server fix held only on the server: a Plane caller, or a server clock running behind the log, could still name an earlier time and reopen an expired grant, with the log's timestamps running backwards. The review's repro: Sam's grant expires 2026-12-19; a read at 2027-01-10 returns 0, and a read named 2026-11-19 appended after it now returns 0 too, with ts 2027-01-10 and its named time in the reason. With the clamp removed the test fails; the `/events` test likewise. ADR 0005 and 0027 carry proposed amendments for the lead.[^1148][^1149][^1150][^1151]

**2026-11-20, RV5, failure.** The first unit test of `syncBeforeRead` found a retire event after a non-owner's read, which looked like the finding still open. **2026-11-20, RV5, failure.** The first in-flight counter for stdio wrapped the transport's `onmessage` after `server.connect`, and missed every request. `connect` starts reading, and input already waiting is read before `connect` returns, through the handler `connect` installed; the wrapper saw no request and the replies drove the counter to -1, so the server closed at once. **2026-11-20, RV5, change.** What runs before a read moved into one core function, `syncBeforeRead`, which the HTTP read route (so `engram read` and `engram mcp`) and the pi extension's `before_agent_start` call (finding RV-SRF-1). The read route swept the store's scope as its owner at the request's `at` for every reader, so a reader refused by `POST /retain` could still retire the owner's items by naming a future time. Before the fix, three of the four RV-SRF-1 tests in `packages/server/test/rv5.test.ts` failed: a non-owner's read with `at` 2030 appended a retire event made by `person:dana`. After it, a non-owner's read sweeps nothing, the owner's read sweeps only at the server's clock, and a future `at` retires nothing; all four pass, with three unit tests of the core function. **2026-11-20, RV5, change.** The server stamps every event's ts from its own clock; only a read takes `at`, as a read-only `valid_at` that moves validity windows and nothing else (finding RV-SRF-2). A request's `at` was its event's ts, so a read backdated to before a grant's expiry returned the granted item and the dogfood report, judging the read at that ts, counted no violation. Eight non-read routes refuse a request naming `at` (400, no event). A read with `at` keeps ts at the server's clock and records the requested time in its reason. A backdated read after a grant expired returns nothing, and `dogfoodReport` counts 0 violations; an honest `valid_at` read inside an item's past validity window is 0 violations too, since the report now judges validity at the recorded time (`packages/core/test/unit/plane/read-time.test.ts`, 4 tests). ADR 0027 has a proposed amendment for the lead; `sdk/openapi.json` regenerated.[^1197][^1198][^1199][^1200][^1201]

**2026-11-20, RV7, decision.** The lead-owned invariants file was extended, only to strengthen it. Invariant 5's grant walk now draws text rewrites by the owner or a co-holder, some moving the item, and checks on every grantee read that each allowed change of an item carrying grants was its owner's. The review asked that what a grantee reads was last written by its owner (RV-CORE-1). Taken literally, that forbids a legitimate flow: a co-holder edits an ungranted item, then the owner grants it. So the check is that the owner wrote it, or granted it afterwards. New guards require owner rewrites of granted items, owner moves, and refused co-holder rewrites and moves. It passes with the fix and fails with both owner rules reverted ("only the owner rewrites an item carrying grants, or moves an item"). Nothing was weakened. For the lead's review of the invariants file.[^1202][^1203]

**2026-11-20, RV7, decision.** The scan after a leading `cd` chain reads quotes, treats `2>&1`, `&>` and `|&` as no separator, and counts a backtick or `$(` inside double quotes as a separator. The finding allowed only `&&` and pipes. Commands like `cd src && grep -r x . 2>&1` are ordinary, while a substitution runs a script whose own `;` the quote scan cannot see. Unterminated quotes and escaped separators also count as separators, so the scan errs towards keeping the cwd. A few ordinary commands with a quoted substitution after a leading `cd` are judged in the cwd too, a cost of blocking too much rather than too little.[^1237]

**2026-11-20, RV7, failure.** Review finding RV7-R7b: the leading `cd dir &&` rule replaced the cwd even when the command went on after a `;`, `||`, a single `&` or a newline. **2026-11-22, E8.12, change, supersedes 2026-11-21-e8-12-change-api-keys.** A correction. The earlier entry said scrypt runs once per key. That is true for a valid key only: a wrong or unknown key pays scrypt on every request. Verification has also changed since. Review findings E8.12-4 and E8.12-5 (the lead chose to keep scrypt, made asynchronous). Verification runs `crypto.scrypt` on the thread pool, where the copied code ran scryptSync. It accepts only r = 8, p = 1, a power-of-two N up to 2^16, and a hash of at least 32 bytes. A p = 64 hash is refused before scrypt runs, and the call returns before scrypt does. Each of those two tests fails under its mutation. Key tests: 13 passed. The `docs/absorbed.md` row and the file header say so. A flood of wrong keys costs thread-pool time, not the event loop.[^1674][^1675][^1676]

**2026-11-22, E8.12, decision.** A stored API key hash is verified only when its scrypt cost N is a power of two no larger than 2^16, with r fixed at 8 and p at 1. The bound was 2^20 before the review fix pass. At 2^20 with r 8, one verification may ask for 1 GiB of memory, so a crafted key file could exhaust the server. The review (finding E8.12-11) noted the lower bound had no decision entry of its own. Keys written by `engram key create` use N 2^14 and still verify, as does 2^16. N 2^17, r 16, p 2 and an N that is not a power of two are refused before scrypt runs, and `maxmem` is set to 256 times N times r. A key file hashed elsewhere at a cost above 2^16 is refused and must be reissued with `engram key create`.[^1689][^1690]

**2026-11-22, E8.12, failure.** The MCP transport's credential check could be skipped with a percent-encoded path. The review found it (E8.12-1, critical); my tests had not. The guard ran on `*` and compared the raw pathname with `/mcp`. Hono routes on the decoded path, so `/%6Dcp` reached the handler with no principal, and the session-owner check was skipped. Before the fix, the regression test reproduced the review's probe. With Dana's key revoked, a `memory_write` to `/%6Dcp` carrying her session id and no Authorization header answered 200 and stored the item, which was attested `insecure_loopback`/`unattributed`. The API was not affected (its guard decodes with `isApiPath`), but it now fails closed too (E8.12-3). A guard keyed on a path is registered on the routed path, and a handler on a server with credentials refuses a request that carries no principal.[^1691][^1692]

The orchestrator changed the test, and this entry records the review: the log events go through `disclosedEvent` over the projection after the promotion and `accessTime(db, when)`, with `when` the promotion's own time, which is the view `promote.ts` builds. A raw answer would still differ from the shown events whenever one is narrowed, so the check still catches a mismatch. `make test-invariants`: 21 passed. The invariant now checks the answer against the log as the promoter may see it.[^2125][^2126][^2127]

**2026-10-29, E1.1, failure.** From PR 2 (E1.1, merged as #10 on 2026-10-29) until this hotfix, a failing test in the core or cli vitest projects could exit 0, so `make test` and CI could not fail on them. Both projects load core's embedded-postgres global setup. Importing embedded-postgres registers async-exit-hook, whose `beforeExit` listener calls `process.exit(0)` on the next tick and overwrote vitest's exit code 1. The bench and adapters projects do not load it and exited 1. Reported by the orchestrating session on 2026-10-29; reproduced here with a temporary failing test in packages/core (exit 0, also with `ENGRAM_PG=skip`, since the import alone registers the hook). With the fix, `make test` on main (65893c9) passes 1720 tests: no test had been failing silently. A regression test now asserts the exit code of a failing run, not only its output.[^2243][^2244][^2245]

**2026-11-03, R1, decision, H4.** The worker cap is an environment variable, `ENGRAM_RESEARCH_WORKERS`, read by `workers()` in `research/scripts/results_io.py`, not a config field. The review (P4A-10) allowed either. The worker count is a property of the machine, not of the experiment: a config field would enter the config the result is regenerated from, and `make test-repro` passes only `--config` and `--out`, so every machine would rerun with the committer's count. The two H4 scripts use it; the other scripts start at most three node processes and are left alone. Unset, the count is one per core, as before, so the committed results are unchanged. If a future script's result depended on its worker count, this cap would hide it; `test_workers.py` guards the two that use it.[^2542][^2543]

**2026-11-03, R1, finding, H1.** The model's requests do not depend on the store, replays on Mem0 take as long as on fake, and Letta's commit per write makes it far slower. Replaying the B3 probe on one store at a time (3 C5 sessions, 474 writes) took 9.8 s on fake, 8.5 on Mem0 and 108 on Letta, once each on a loaded machine: about 0.2 s per Letta write. GateMem's arm writes each checkpoint's turns in each of its 12 sessions: 325,530 turn items (`research/results/h1-c4-verdict-agreement.json`) times 12, about 3.9 million writes, nine days on Letta at that rate. The store changes time and fidelity, not the requests.[^2577][^2578][^2579][^2580]

**2026-11-20, RV6, failure, H1.** The run lock could not tell a reused pid from its holder, took a stale lock over with unlink then create, and a merge did not lock the shard folders it read (review P60-8). The lock recorded only a pid and a host. The lock records its holder's start time and a nonce. A live process of this host whose start time differs by more than 2 s is not the holder; one whose start time cannot be read keeps the lock. A stale lock is renamed to a name of the attempt's own, checked by nonce, and given back if it changed. A merge holds every shard folder's lock. Tests: a live child process with another start time loses the lock and with its own keeps it; a shard resume during a merge is refused. A reused pid no longer blocks a run.[^2859][^2860]

**2026-11-20, RV6, failure, H1.** The lock took its holder's start as Date.now() minus ps etimes, at one second resolution (verifier finding P60-R2). A clock step of more than 2 s during a long run made a live holder's start differ from the lock's, so the lock was judged gone: the one way it failed open. The start is now absolute: /proc/<pid>/stat starttime plus btime on Linux, ps lstart elsewhere, CIM on Windows as before. The reader is injectable (lockedBy and the journal's startOf). Tests: a matching holder is kept, a mismatching one taken over, an unreadable one kept; the parser is checked. Both mutations fail them. A clock step no longer frees a live lock by itself; btime is derived from the clock on Linux, so a step between the lock's write and its read can still shift it, which the 2 s slack does not cover.[^2861][^2862]

A flag set when the merge starts writing the folder now gates the cleanup. Test: a good run in the folder survives a merge refused by a shard lock of another host. Mutation: gating on sealed again fails it. A refused lock leaves the folder as it was.[^2863][^2864]

**2026-11-20, RV6, change.** A run journal holds `run.lock` in its output folder, naming its process id and host, from open to close; a second journal on the folder is refused (`JournalLocked`). The RV1 backlog row "Concurrent writers" (`docs/log/2026-11-19-rv1-finding-concurrent-writers.md`): two processes on one `--out` interleave their rows, and sharding makes several processes the normal case. The lock is created with an exclusive open. A lock whose holder, on this host, no longer runs (signal 0) is taken over; another host's lock, or one naming no process, is refused with the path to remove. The journal releases the lock when it closes, after a crash inside the run too. A merge refuses a shard folder whose lock is held. Tested in `rv6.test.ts` ("one process at a time writes a folder"). The backlog row is closed by this card.[^2865][^2866]

**2026-11-21, B10, change.** Card B10 adds the cassette proxy of ADR 0036 to `@engram/model`: `startProxy` serves `POST /v1/chat/completions` on 127.0.0.1 through `cached()`, keyed by `cacheKey`, the function the runner's calls are keyed by. MERIT (H2) and tau2-bench (H5) call their models through LiteLLM, outside rules 6 and 7; the proxy brings those calls under the same cache without porting either harness. Replay is the default and a miss is a 404 `cassette_miss` returned and kept in `errors`; `new_episodes` records from an injected upstream and is refused under ENGRAM_OFFLINE=1; usage goes to `onUsage` as the runner's UsageRecord; streaming and embeddings return 501. The acceptance command passes 17 tests, among them a first run of 3 new calls, then a second run and a replay of 0 new calls with byte-identical bodies. **2026-11-21, B10, finding, supersedes 2026-11-21-b10-finding-for-harness-cards.** What cards B7 and B11 must add around the proxy, restated after review. The proxy is a library in `@engram/model`, which may not import the runner (ADR 0033), so the runner's folders and ledger are the caller's. (1) Pick the folder with `liveConfig` or `replayConfig`; run `recordingRefusal` on it before `fileCache`, which creates its folder; pass `repo` and the journal's `onUsage`. (2) No live upstream exists yet: a ChatCall on pi-ai that sends the seed. (3) LiteLLM strips its provider prefix, so the model the proxy sees must be `provider/model-id`. **2026-11-21, E1.5, failure.** The first simulation of the good model reported a violation of noStaleAppend at seed 1 (2,000 traces of 40 steps). A writer's own bytes had been adopted before it committed, which the code's check ignores by content (commit.ts ownBytes). The later erasure redacted the content of both events, so the property, reading the log afterwards, could no longer match them. The protocol was right and the property was wrong. Each event now carries a ghost field `orig`, its content as appended, which no step reads and only the properties do. The same seed then passed, and 5,000 traces at each of three seeds passed. A property that reads past events has to read them as they were appended, not as redaction left them.[^3086]

Every parameter sent is listed: `wafer/us` takes seed, tools, reasoning, temperature, max_tokens, response_format and structured_outputs; GPT-5.4 on `openai` takes seed, tools and reasoning (no temperature, which its answer turns never send); both judges take theirs. 20 of 20 pass. Mutation: an answer turn that also sends temperature fails B1's pin; restored. A dropped parameter now stops the run at its first call (card X20) instead of passing silently.[^3315][^3316][^3317][^3318][^3319]

**2026-11-27, R6, change, H1.** Sections 7 and 8 of the runbook ran the smoke run and both H1 arms with `MODEL=openrouter/openai/gpt-5.6-terra`. Since R6 the runner refuses any model but a pinned config's `answer_model`, so each would be refused. They now name M1, `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` (lead-decisions item 1), and the cassette folder reads `cassettes-upstream-<hash>`. The answer turn's sent parameters list `max_tokens`, which pi-ai always sends; both pinned endpoints support it (23 of 23 pass). The verification of the fix pass found the smoke command refused; the H1 commands had the same fault. No `MODEL=` in the runbook names `gpt-5.6-terra`. The cost configs still price that model; the backlog row on the smoke run's price keeps that open. The commands run as written.[^3320][^3321][^3322]

**2026-11-27, R6, change, H1.** The four endpoint responses of 2026-11-26 are committed as served under `research/configs/openrouter-endpoints/2026-11-26/`, and each snapshot entry names its file (`response`) and now records every endpoint's full `supported_parameters`. A new test hashes each file against `response_sha256` and rebuilds every endpoint entry from it. Biome skips the folder, since a reformat would change the hashed bytes. Review finding 7: the hash named responses nobody could read, and the `seed` flags were transcribed by hand. Finding 2 needs the full parameter lists. 20 of 20 tests pass. Mutation: setting DeepSeek's own endpoint to `seed: true` fails the rebuild test and the rule's pin tests; restored. Every seed flag and price in the snapshot can be checked offline.[^3323][^3324][^3325][^3326][^3327]

**2026-11-27, R6, change, H1.** Three fixes to the endpoint test. It now takes each config's judge from `judgeModel`, which `live.ts` now exports. That is how the runner resolves the judge: the config's own, or else the benchmark's paper judge. The lint configs' test now requires their pin instead of returning early. The header states the seed-first rule. Review findings 5, 6 and 9. A config that dropped its explicit judge and its judge pin passed while the run would call GPT-4o unpinned, and deleting the lint pins kept the test green. 20 of 20 pass. Mutations: removing `judge` and the judge pin from `h1-gatemem.json` fails that config's test. Removing the pin from `l3-pilot.json` fails the lint test. Both were restored from the index. The test now pins what the runner calls, not just what each config spells out.[^3328][^3329][^3330]

**2026-11-27, R6, change, H1.** Two wording fixes. The backlog row "OpenRouter endpoints in the configs" now says the endpoint list was the one card RV6 could not read offline. A new failure entry supersedes `2026-11-26-r6-failure-first-m1-pin-without-seed.md` and attributes the seed-first rule to the lead's own answer of 2026-11-26. Review findings 8 and 9. Once R6 marked the row done, "this card" read as R6. The old entry credited the coordinator with a rule the lead answered directly, and the thesis has to report correctly who changed registered text. Log entries are immutable (`docs/conventions/documentation.md`, rule 5), so the old entry stays as it is. Text only. No code, config or result changed. The thesis's account of the Models rule cites the lead.[^3331][^3332]

**2026-11-27, R6, decision, H1.** R6 merges on its gates and its five reachable MANIFEST rows (h1-cost, h1-check-runs-cost, h2-cost-table, h2-longmemeval-cost and h3-lint-floor, each rerun alone and matching its committed sha256). The full `make test-repro` runs once, at X20's head after main with R6 is merged into it, before X20 merges and before the tag. The runner change in R6 is in the live path only, which no research script takes, and a full run takes about three hours on this machine. One run at the later head covers R6's code as well. R6's gates: `make lint` 0, `make lint-docs` 0, `make test` 0 (vitest 6,729 passed; pytest 561 passed). A row that fails at X20's head because of R6 is fixed in a PR before the tag.[^3333][^3334]

**2026-11-27, R6, failure, H1, supersedes 2026-11-26-r6-failure-first-m1-pin-without-seed.** The first pin of M1 (commit `1468a2b9`) took DeepSeek's own endpoint, tag `deepseek`, by the rule's first branch read literally, although that endpoint does not honour `seed`. The rule named the maker's endpoint first and put the `seed` condition only on its second branch. The conflict with AGENTS.md rule 6 was written down as a note instead of being settled. The independent review raised it (finding R6-3). The lead answered on 2026-11-26, "Seed first", directly and not under the delegation (`docs/tasks/lead-decisions.md`, "The lead's answers, 2026-11-26", answer B). A maker's endpoint without `seed` does not qualify. Commit `7ca9cd60` moved every M1 pin to `wafer/us`, and the test checks that every pinned endpoint honours `seed`. This entry corrects the superseded one, which wrongly said "the coordinator decided" (review finding 8). No run used the first pin, so there is nothing to undo outside this branch.[^3335][^3336][^3337]

**2026-11-27, R6, failure, H1.** `make lint-docs` failed on three of the fix pass's entries, each over the 150-word limit for a body (159, 152 and 171 words). They were written as complete entries and never counted. Each was shortened on this branch before merge, with no fact dropped but the service tiers the listing gives OpenAI's endpoints. `make lint-docs` passes. None outside this branch.[^3338][^3339][^3340][^3341]

**2026-11-27, X20, change, H1.** The closed backlog row "A refused answer call" now lists the stop set as built: 401, 402, 403 and 404 at any model call, the moderation 403 as an exception, the reason name `answer refused`, and the five-item backstop. It cites the lead's answer of 2026-11-26. The final review's finding 9. The row was marked done but still gave the old set, "an HTTP 401, 402 or 403". One row changed in `docs/tasks/backlog.md`. The backlog and pre-tag condition 3 agree.[^3342]

**2026-11-27, X20, change, H1.** `research/analysis/h1.py` gives two new errors. A utility row that has an exclusion and also a verdict is refused with "a refused utility session has no utility verdict". A utility row with a violation is refused with "a utility session has no violation". The final review's finding 7. Since X20 a utility row may carry an exclusion, so the old message "a utility session has no violation and no exclusion" was no longer true in either check. The test now matches the new message. It failed before the fix and passes after. test_h1_answer_refused, test_h1_exclusions, test_h1_secondary and test_h1_pipeline: 22 passed. Error text only. No result bytes move.[^3343][^3344]

**2026-11-27, X20, change, H1.** At MEM-INV-Bench's note call, a 401, 402, 404 or non-moderation 403 that stops the run, and each retried transient attempt, now write one ledger line with the attempt's usage. That is `attemptUsage` under the call's key, as at the answer call. The final review's finding 6, and card step 4: every failed attempt's usage goes to the ledger once. Such a reply can carry a cost. pi-ai folds a mid-stream error body's `"code": 402` into the message after tokens were streamed, and `stoppingStatus` reads that code. A new test answers 429 and then 402: the run stops, nothing is recorded, and the ledger has two lines under one key. With the stop's line removed, the test fails (1 line, not 2). x1-mem-inv and mem-inv-probe: 33 of 33. No replay moves. The line is written only on the live path.[^3345][^3346]

**2026-11-27, X20, change, H1.** The backstop's stop message now says that the five items' refusals are recorded in the cassettes, so RESUME=1 replays them as refused, and names the manual remedy: delete those items' cassette entries that begin with the refused-answer mark, cut their rows from the end of results.jsonl (and events.jsonl for GateMem), then resume. The final review's finding 4: the old message said "check the provider, then rerun with RESUME=1", which brings none of the five back if the cause was a misread provider failure. A new test follows the remedy and the resume asks all six items again (12 calls, none refused). The runner README and the H1 runbook (`prereg-v1-plan.md`, section 7) say the same. answer-refusal.test.ts: 27 of 27. The operator has a documented way back after a misread.[^3347][^3348][^3349][^3350]

**2026-11-27, X20, finding, H1.** Excluding every non-retryable 400 at the answer call breaks two tests of card RV1, and X20's acceptance requires `rv1.test.ts` to pass unchanged. `rv1.test.ts:92` ("a failure that is not transient still fails the run") and `rv1-review.test.ts:238` ("is not retried by the outer loop") answer the call with `400 Bad Request` and expect the run to reject. Under the 400 rule the session is excluded and the run ends normally. With the rule applied (`leading === 400` and no key or credit words), `vitest run` over rv1, rv1-review, judge and x1-mem-inv gave 2 failed, 61 passed; the code was then restored. The branch keeps the old 400 reading. For the orchestrator: either change those two tests to use a non-transient error with no 400 status, which changes the acceptance's "unchanged", or keep the plain 400 as a stop.[^3351][^3352][^3353]

**2026-11-27, X20, finding.** No passing `make test-repro` is recorded for X20. The failure entry `2026-11-26-x20-failure-test-repro-timeout.md` says the rerun is "in the report and PR.md". That rerun was never logged, and PR.md is not committed. The final review's finding 8. The fix pass of 2026-11-27 does not run `make test-repro`, because the orchestrator runs it serially before the merge to keep load off the shared machine. The only evidence on the branch is the first run's ten matching rows out of 25. No MANIFEST row, fixture or cassette is touched by the branch (`git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` names none). The orchestrator's serial `make test-repro` at the final head is the acceptance evidence. It goes in a measurement entry that names the head, the rows reproduced and the worker count.[^3354][^3355]

**2026-11-28, change.** `research/scripts/consolidate_log.py` no longer holds a superseded entry to the measurement rules, and `make thesis` rebuilt `research/thesis/drafts/`. Entries are immutable, so a measurement entry with no MANIFEST results file or bare config path can only be corrected by superseding it; before, the old entry still failed validation and blocked every draft. Before: a superseded measurement was checked for its MANIFEST row and config like a current one. After: it is still checked for its fields, values, body and evidence paths, and is left out of every draft as before. Two tests pin it: a superseded measurement without a config consolidates, and a superseded entry with a missing evidence path is still refused. Rule 5 of `docs/conventions/documentation.md` says so. The drafts are current as of 2026-11-28.[^3368][^3369][^3370][^3371]

No single page said which research results exist, what each answers, whether it is a hypothesis result, and which entries record it. Before: results were findable only through `research/results/MANIFEST.md` and the log. After: one section per MANIFEST row, grouped by hypothesis, each with its question, status, pre-registration section, headline values read from the file with their key paths, and its current measurement entries; a top section says no hypothesis has a result yet and what H1 to H5 still need. `research/tests/test_results_register.py` keeps the register current.[^3372][^3373][^3374][^3375][^3376][^3377]

An edit to the config is formatted with biome before commit.[^3382][^3383]

Six were already superseded, but the script held superseded entries to the same rules, so rule 5's only correction could not clear them. The script now skips the measurement rules for a superseded entry (tested in `research/tests/test_consolidate.py`), and fourteen 2026-11-28 entries supersede the other fourteen.
